away.name: Stuart Skinner
away.news: Skinner has been stellar early in his tenure with the Jets and will return to the crease on Thursday. The 27-year-old Canadian goalie stopped 19 of 21 shots (.905 SV%) in his most recent outing, a 5-2 win over the Minnesota Wild. He has a 2.47 GAA and .917 SV% in four games this season (3-1-0). The Jets enter action on Thursday as -126 road favourites against a Chicago Blackhawks team coming off a season-high five-goal output in a 5-3 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins.

home.name: Spencer Knight
home.news: The Blackhawks welcomed Connor Bedard (shoulder) back into the lineup for his season debut in a 5-3 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins, a bright note in an otherwise disappointing 2-5-0 start to the season. The team hopes to build on the momentum of their superstar captain's return, turning to Knight to tend the twine on Thursday. The 25-year-old Knight had a solid first full season in Chicago, but has a subpar 3.64 GAA and .885 SV% through five games this season (2-3-0). Chicago enters Thursday's contest as +114 home underdogs against a surprising 4-1-1 Winnipeg Jets team.

away.name: Alex Nedeljkovic
away.news: Yaroslav Askarov's start to the season has been underwhelming, posting an ugly 3.99 GAA and .848 SV% in five games (2-3-0), which makes Nedeljkovic's lack of action this season somewhat surprising. The 30-year-old Nedeljkovic was excellent in his only outing this season, saving 24 of 26 shots (.923 SV%) in a 3-2 overtime win over the St. Louis Blues. The Sharks enter Thursday as +121 road underdogs against a Nashville Predators team that has lost three of its last four (1-3-0).

home.name: Juuse Saros
home.news: With Justus Annunen still navigating an undisclosed injury, the Predators will continue to rely on Saros. Saros is coming off his worst performance in the young 2026-27 season, allowing five goals on 25 shots (.800 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights. The 31-year-old Finnish goalie has a 3.17 GAA and .897 SV% in five games (2-2-1). The Predators enter Thursday as -135 home favourites against a San Jose Sharks team that has scored just seven goals in its last four games (1-3-0).

away.name: Joel Hofer
away.news: Hofer led the Blues onto the ice for warmups.

home.name: Jesper Wallstedt
home.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined, and he got his first night off in Minnesota's previous game, but the team fared poorly without him, losing 5-2 to the Winnipeg Jets. Wallstedt emerged as Minnesota's starting goalie in the playoffs and has carried that momentum into the 2026-27 season. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has an outstanding 1.82 GAA and .933 SV% in six games (4-1-1). Minnesota enters Thursday's contest as -140 home favourites against a St. Louis Blues team on a two-game winning streak.

away.name: Karel Vejmelka
away.news: Vejmelka hasn't been outstanding this season, but his 4-1-0 record has helped Utah get off to a strong start. The 30-year-old Czech goalie allowed four goals on 26 shots (.846 SV%) in his most recent game, but received enough goal support to salvage a 5-4 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. He has a 2.46 GAA and .895 SV% this season. The Mammoth enter Thursday's contest as slight -112 road favourites against the high-flying Edmonton Oilers, who average 4.8 goals per game through six games this season (5-0-1).

home.name: Devon Levi
home.news: The Oilers have struggled between the pipes in recent seasons, but they hope Levi can provide long-overdue stability after a promising start to the 2026-27 season. The 24-year-old Levi has yet to lose in four games this season (4-0-0), posting a 2.76 GAA and .903 SV%, and is coming off an outstanding performance, saving 39 of 40 shots (.975 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Los Angeles Kings. The Oilers enter Thursday's contest as slight -110 home favourites against a Central Division-leading Utah Mammoth team that has scored 27 goals (3.9 GF/GP) in seven games (5-2-0).

away.name: Dustin Wolf
away.news: After a 0-5-0 start, the Flames hope to build momentum off their first win of the season, improving to 1-5-0. Wolf was instrumental in the win, saving 23 of 25 shots (.920 SV%) to defeat the Anaheim Ducks 4-2. The 25-year-old American goalie has a 4.56 GAA and .839 SV% in four games (1-3-0). The Flames enter Thursday’s contest as significant +266 road underdogs against a 6-2-0 Vegas Golden Knights team.

home.name: Carter Hart
home.news: After leading Vegas to the Stanley Cup Finals last season, Hart has been favoured between the pipes early in the 2026-27 season and will return to the crease on Thursday. The 28-year-old goalie allowed three goals on 27 shots (.889 SV%) in his most recent game, a 4-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild. He has a 2.41 GAA and .906 SV% in five games (3-2-0). The Golden Knights enter Thursday's contest as significant -308 home favourites against a Calgary Flames team that has only scored 12 goals this season (1-5-0).
